To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority (90%) of mothers had institutional deliveries and 75.6 % of infants were breastfed within the first hour after delivery.
the prevalence of low birth weight, early initiation of breastfeeding, and exclusive breastfeeding are high in rural areas of Rajahmundry.
the prevalence of low birth weight, exclusive breastfeeding, and complementary feeding were 12.5%, 79.1%, and 50.7% respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the factors that influence the infant feeding practices and the role of maternal factors in determining the infant feeding practices.
the need for the improvement of the health of the infant and child population by promoting the healthy infant feeding practices.
identifying and understanding the factors that affect the infant and child feeding and caring practices in rural population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prevalence of safe infant feeding practices is still low among mothers in rural areas of Rajamahendravarapadu.
the infant feeding practices are suboptimal in the rural areas of Rajamahendravaram.
the prevalence of faulty infant feeding practices is high in rural Rajamandhry district.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study has shown the need of a community-based intervention programme for promoting safe intra and infant feeding practices in rural areas.
the prevalence of low birth weight and preterm births is still high in rural areas and the proportion of exclusive breast feeding is still low.
the majority of the mothers were aware of the benefits of breastfeeding but the actual practice was not as good as the awareness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the working mothers with lower education are more vulnerable to faulty infant feeding practices.
the health education and awareness of the mothers should be given utmost importance to ensure the healthy growth and development of children.
there is a significant association between maternal literacy and work status and infant feeding practices.
